utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm one of the doctors. I understand you've got burning when you wee since yesterday. I'm sorry you're dealing with that. Before I examine you, can you tell me a bit more about how it started and exactly what you're feeling?
reply: It started yesterday morning and has been getting worse. It stings and burns, especially at the end when I wee. I've been going all the time, every half hour or so, but only pass a little each time. The urine is a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

awards.label: How long the symptoms have been present

utterance: Thank you, that's helpful. A few more questions: Have you had any fever, chills, shivering, feeling generally unwell, or pain in your back or the sides of your tummy? And any tummy pain lower down, or feeling sick/vomiting?
reply: No, I haven't had any fever, chills, shivering or feeling generally unwell. I don't have pain in my back or sides, just a bit of a low ache above my bladder. I'm eating normally and haven't been sick or felt nauseous.

utterance: Have you noticed any itching, irritation, unusual discharge from the vagina, or a smell down below? And could you be pregnant at the moment?
reply: No, I haven't noticed any itching, irritation or unusual discharge from the vagina, and there's no strange smell down there. I don't think I'm pregnant.

utterance: When you've had a UTI before, how were you treated, and did it clear up? Have you had any problems with your kidneys, or anything like kidney stones?
reply: I had a UTI about two years ago and it was treated with antibiotics, and it cleared up. I don't have any known problems with my kidneys or bladder, or anything like kidney stones.

utterance: Can you tell me the first day of your last period, and are your periods regular? That helps me check anything pregnancy-related.
reply: The first day of my last period was about two weeks ago, and my periods are regular.

utterance: I also need to ask a few sensitive questions because some infections passed between partners can cause burning. Have you had a new sexual partner in the last few months, or more than one partner recently? And have you noticed any pain deep inside during sex or any bleeding after sex?
reply: I've been with the same boyfriend for about a year, and he's the only one. I haven't had any pain during sex or bleeding after sex, and nothing between my periods.

awards.label: Bleeding after sex or between periods

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: The findings and your urine test are very much in keeping with a bladder infection — what we call cystitis. A quick dipstick of your urine showed white cells and nitrites, which strongly suggest a bacterial infection in the bladder. I've also sent a sample to the lab to grow the bacteria and confirm the best antibiotic; that takes a couple of days.
reply: I'm glad you think it's a bladder infection. I was pretty sure it was a UTI again. I just need antibiotics to get rid of it so I can go back to work.

utterance: I'm giving you a 3-day course of an antibiotic called trimethoprim — one 300 mg tablet once a day for three days. Please take all of the tablets even if you feel better sooner. Drink plenty of water, and you can take paracetamol if you're uncomfortable. You should start to feel better within a day or two.
reply: I'll take the antibiotics as prescribed and make sure to drink plenty of water. I'll also take paracetamol if needed. I'm hoping to feel better soon so I can get back to work.

utterance: Please come back or seek medical care sooner if you develop a fever, shakes or chills, pain in your back or side, vomiting, feel faint or more unwell, see blood in your urine, or if the burning hasn't improved within 48 hours. Also return if your symptoms come back after the course. In the meantime, simple measures like not holding on for too long, wiping front to back, drinking plenty of water, and passing urine after sex can help prevent future infections. Your antibiotic doesn't affect your contraceptive pill.
reply: I'll make sure to come back if any of those things happen. I'll try to drink more water and pass urine after sex. I'm glad the antibiotic won't affect my pill.

awards.label: Reasonable differential: Urethritis from a sexually transmitted infection
